en: Contrary to the belief that it is a simple mountain, Taal is a complex volcano featuring a main crater inside a lake inside a larger caldera.
Despite outdated textbooks claiming 7,107 islands, updated NAMRIA mapping confirms the Philippine archipelago actually consists of 7,641 individual islands.
Contrary to popular belief about the Pasig, the Cagayan River is actually the longest and largest river in the Philippines.
Many mistakenly assume Manila is the largest city, but Davao City actually holds the title for the largest total land area.
Unlike regular water buffaloes that roam many islands, the endangered Tamaraw is a unique dwarf buffalo found exclusively on the island of Mindoro.
Contrary to the assumption of a single tropical weather pattern, the Philippines actually experiences four distinct climate types based on rainfall distribution.
Although geographically closer to the Visayas, Palawan is administratively classified under the MIMAROPA region of the Luzon island group, not the Visayas.
The West Philippine Sea is not a completely separate ocean, but the official local designation for the eastern parts of the South China Sea.
Many mistakenly believe Laguna de Bay is the deepest, but Lake Lanao in Mindanao is actually the deepest lake in the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were not built by Spanish colonizers, but were actually carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is not located near the Palawan mainland, but actually sits entirely within the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Unlike neighboring Indonesia, the Equator line does not cross through the Philippines, which actually lies entirely north of it within the Northern Hemisphere.
